acceptance_signals: Recheck the retained wheel filename, SHA-256, distribution identity, predecessor task hashes, and absence of running task Python processes before consumer preparation.
Create exactly one fresh operating-system temporary task root containing one disposable local Git repository with no remote and one fresh Python 3.11 environment.
Install the retained 0.3.0rc1 wheel offline with no index and no dependencies; perform no dependency or package download.
Verify the installed packaged Codex MCP binding enables all expected tools including agentgov_task_completion_record and declares the 1800-second timeout without writing any real consumer repository.

Launch only the installed foreground STDIO Adapter from the disposable repository and send controlled MCP initialize and tools/list messages for a client without form elicitation and a client with form elicitation.
Observe Adapter 1.7.0, six base tools, eight form-capable tools, completion input only task_path, clean JSON-RPC output, and normal process exit with no remaining task process.

Do not start Codex or another model, call any AgentGov tool, create a consumer task or completion record, alter consumer product content, access a real consumer repository, repair product source, retry after a product deviation, or clean retained evidence.
Do not modify Starter source, tests, or predecessor records; update only the newly admitted task evidence and named current-state documentation.
Run every declared validation command, record deterministic results, and perform a separate bounded current-Agent review without claiming native self-review completion.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-542b3ee7e39a4aa6a2be756bf2fa0f75 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Use the retained verified AgentGov 0.3.0rc1 wheel to create one fresh remote-free disposable consumer repository and one fresh Python 3.11 environment. Install the exact wheel offline, verify the packaged Codex MCP binding includes the completion tool and 1800-second timeout, then launch the installed foreground STDIO Adapter in controlled no-model processes and verify initialize plus tools/list for six base and eight form-capable tools. Stop before any model or completion-tool call.

items: A malformed STDIO driver could misclassify a harness failure as an Adapter failure; messages and exit conditions must be deterministic and privacy-bounded.
A foreground Adapter process could remain running after a failed exchange; process identity and final absence must be checked without broad termination.
The disposable repository could be confused with a real consumer; it must resolve inside the fresh task temporary root and have no remote.
The retained wheel could have changed after prior validation; any identity or digest mismatch must stop before installation.
The dirty Starter worktree contains prior user and task changes that must remain classified and preserved.
Reviewed assumption: The retained verified wheel and its isolated build evidence remain readable.
Reviewed assumption: Python 3.11 and Git are available locally.
Reviewed assumption: The installed Adapter needs no runtime dependency beyond the wheel for controlled initialize and tools/list exchanges.
Reviewed assumption: This is a fully specified low-risk successor selected from the preceding completion review and needs no new product alignment.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the installed console entry point starts and completes clean STDIO MCP exchanges from a disposable consumer working directory.
Reviewed unknown: Whether process-level capability negotiation returns the same six and eight tool inventories observed in isolated in-process discovery.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the packaged Codex binding and installed runtime identities remain consistent in the disposable consumer context.

title: Disposable consumer STDIO discovery v1
